body: Tuesday, February 03 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information cutoff: 2026-02-03 00:00 UTC. Market figures use completed observations before this date.

Macro Stance: Bullish on growth, bearish on duration. The January ISM manufacturing PMI jumped to 52.6% PR Newswire [Feb 02], the fastest gains since 2022 WSJ [Feb 02], and the S&P 500 flirted with a record high as chipmakers and small caps jumped Reuters [Feb 02]. The catch: the January employment report will be delayed by the partial government shutdown Reuters [Feb 02], so the market is trading one survey and a hawkish Fed pick without its main labour gauge.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.57% and the 10Y at 4.29%, a 72 bps 10Y−2Y spread; over 20 observations both rose 10 bps on rounded figures, a move classed as bear steepening (both up, 10Y up more) that leaves the curve moderately steep, approaching the long-run average (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-02). Over five observations the 10Y rose 7 bps against 1 bp for the 2Y (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-02). The S&P 500 closed at 6,976.44, up 0.54%, with the VIX down 1.1 points to 16.34 and the DXY up 0.64% to 97.61 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

New / Most Important: Treasury yields ticked higher on the strong data as traders weighed the Warsh pick CNBC [Feb 02], whom they read as the more hawkish choice Bloomberg.com [Jan 30]. Washington also agreed to cut tariffs on India to 18% after India agreed to end Russian oil purchases Reuters [Feb 02] — a trade de-escalation that removes one inflation risk while the shutdown blinds the Fed's labour read. Stronger factories, a tougher chair and missing payrolls together argue for owning cyclicals while keeping duration light.

Playbook ✓: Own cyclicals over duration: industrials, small caps — IWM closed at 262.18, up 1.02% — and banks, and stay underweight TLT, which fell 0.67% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Add duration only if the 10Y falls back below 4.19%, its level 20 observations earlier (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-02); cut cyclicals if the delayed payrolls fail to confirm the ISM jump.

Macro Stance: Bullish. Banks drove European stocks to a record high as markets recovered from a rocky start Reuters [Feb 02]: the STOXX 600 closed at 617.31, up 1.03%, and the FTSE 100 at 10,341.60, up 1.16% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Germany's manufacturing sector is showing signs of recovery, the PMI indicates Reuters [Feb 02].

Activity & Inflation: The cycle is turning at the factory gate, but margins are not: euro-zone firms see deteriorating profits, the ECB's access-to-finance survey shows Reuters [Feb 02]. Volume up and pricing power down is the mix that keeps the ECB on hold rather than hiking, and it argues for owning lenders over price-takers. Germany's PMI turn Reuters [Feb 02] matters most because it has been the region's laggard.

New / Most Important: Reuters frames the ECB meeting around five questions under the banner 'no escaping the euro or the Fed' Reuters [Feb 02]. EUR/USD fell 0.97% to 1.1849 as the dollar rebounded and the DAX rose 1.05% to 24,797.52 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02) — a softer euro eases the squeeze on exporters.

Playbook ✓: Stay long euro-area banks and domestic cyclicals — the record was bank-led Reuters [Feb 02] — and add selectively to exporters while EUR/USD holds below 1.1849 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Trim banks if the ECB signals enough concern about corporate margins to hint at a cut, which would flatten curves and hit net interest income.

Macro Stance: Bearish. Factory data split — the official manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.3 Reuters [Jan 30] while a private gauge showed expansion for export-oriented firms Bloomberg.com [Feb 02] — but property, land revenue and markets all deteriorated. Policy is easing at the margin, not by enough to offset a housing relapse that drags on household confidence and local budgets.

PMIs & Activity: The official PMI at 49.3 Reuters [Jan 30] reflects soft domestic orders, while the private gauge for export-oriented firms expanded Bloomberg.com [Feb 02]. The split says exporters are coping and the domestic economy is not; confirmation of a broader turn needs the official gauge back above 50 after the Lunar New Year distortions wash out.

Credit Impulse: No January credit print is in the feed yet. Price is moving instead of volume: the PBOC's key bank loan rate fell to a record low Bloomberg.com [Feb 02], which helps willing borrowers but does not create demand from households that are deleveraging. A rebound in January new loans and social financing is what would confirm an impulse.

Property: The January relief rally is fading: SCMP reports a 'bleak start' to 2026 as property sales declines accelerate South China Morning Post [Feb 02], and local governments logged a double-digit drop in land-sale income for a fourth straight year in 2025 一财全球Yicai Global [Feb 02]. Lower land revenue squeezes local budgets exactly where infrastructure support would have to come from.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Fiscal support stays narrow: with land income shrinking 一财全球Yicai Global [Feb 02], Beijing is leaning on monetary plumbing rather than budget stimulus. Externally, Xi's 'strong currency' mission to make the yuan a global reserve South China Morning Post [Jan 31] rules out a devaluation to rescue exporters; USD/CNY held at 6.9510, down 0.6% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Markets & Flows: Hong Kong stocks dropped by the most since November, led by mining and telecoms South China Morning Post [Feb 02]: the Hang Seng closed at 26,775.57, down 2.23%, and the Shanghai Composite at 4,015.75, down 2.48% and now 0.19% lower over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). ASHR is down 0.72%, KWEB 1.57% and FXI 1.63% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02) — January's gains are gone.

New / Most Important: The metals crash transmitted straight into Hong Kong, where mining led the drop South China Morning Post [Feb 02], and property sales are weakening again South China Morning Post [Feb 02]. Together they suggest the late-January rally on eased developer rules was a positioning trade that has run its course, while the record-low loan rate Bloomberg.com [Feb 02] shows Beijing still prefers incremental easing to a big stimulus.

Playbook ✓: Underweight China beta (FXI, ASHR) and avoid developers; keep only exporter and AI-hardware exposure that the private PMI supports. Turn constructive if the official PMI returns above 50 and January credit data rebound; cut further if the Hang Seng loses 26,347.24, its level 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). ⚠ Divergence: the private factory gauge for exporters is expanding Bloomberg.com [Feb 02] and the PBOC loan rate is at a record low Bloomberg.com [Feb 02] — if exporters keep hiring, the bearish property story may overstate the hit to listed earnings.

Macro Stance: Bullish. A survey shows the LDP-JIP coalition on track for a two-thirds majority The Japan Times [Feb 02], and the BOJ's January summary showed members debating the risk of falling behind the curve on inflation Reuters [Feb 01]. A supermajority plus a hawkish-leaning central bank is a reflation mix for domestic earnings and for banks.

Activity & Currency: USD/JPY rose 1.33% to 155.20 after Takaichi's comment cooled intervention speculation The Japan Times [Feb 02], while the Nikkei 225 fell 1.25% to 52,655.18 but is still up 4.6% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Reuters notes Takaichi must face bond investors before she wins over voters Reuters [Feb 02], so fiscal promises are being priced in the JGB curve.

Playbook ✓: Own exporters again on a weaker yen and keep domestic banks for the BOJ angle, while hedging long-end JGB exposure into the vote. Cut if USD/JPY reverses its 1.33% one-day rise (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02) on renewed intervention talk, or if bond investors force a fiscal retreat.

Macro Stance: Bearish for domestic equities. A rate hike is expected at Tuesday's RBA meeting ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation [Jan 29], a U-turn that breaks from the global easing trend Bloomberg.com [Feb 01], and market experts are pricing higher odds of an increase Mortgage Professional America [Feb 02]. Tightening into a strong currency raises the hurdle for the whole market.

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD fell 1.43% to 0.6946 as the dollar rebounded but is still up 3.93% over 20 sessions, while the ASX 200 fell 1.02% to 8,778.60 and is up only 0.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). The currency has done part of the RBA's tightening, and equities have stopped rewarding good news.

Playbook ✓: Underweight rate-sensitive ASX sectors into the decision and prefer bank margins over housing-linked names. A hike with a hawkish statement should lift AUD again; a hold would push it toward 0.6684, its level 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), and favour ASX rate-sensitives on relief.

Monetary & Activity: Poland's manufacturing PMI edged up in January, with industry optimism at its highest in years, Rzeczpospolita reports Rzeczpospolita [Feb 02]. MPC member Kotecki has said a cut could come as early as February Bloomberg.com [Jan 16] — easing into an improving factory cycle, the best mix for domestic equities.

FX & Markets: The zloty weakened with the dollar rebound: USD/PLN rose 1.17% to 3.5548 and EUR/PLN closed at 4.2117; EPOL added 0.19%, PKO BP 0.99% and Pekao 2.12%, while KGHM fell 5.99% and is down 12.25% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Money.pl reports KGHM lost 15% at the open as the metals selloff hit the Warsaw floor Money.pl [Feb 02].

Companies: Remigiusz Paszkiewicz now runs KGHM Rzeczpospolita [Feb 02], so the stock trades on copper and silver rather than on the leadership change. Allegro is under fire, with Erli filing a lawsuit after InPost Bankier.pl [Feb 02]; ALE rose 1.69% in the prior session but is down 4.9% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Security & New Development: Poland picked a Kongsberg-PGZ consortium to build its anti-drone 'wall' Defense News [Feb 02], channelling defence spending to a domestic partner. With a February cut possible Bloomberg.com [Jan 16], fiscal and monetary policy both lean pro-growth.

Playbook ✓: Own PKO BP and Pekao for growth and dividends and keep zloty exposure while EUR/PLN holds near 4.21 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02); re-enter KGHM only after copper, down 1.62% to 5.80, stabilises. ⚠ Divergence: the PMI shows the best industry optimism in years Rzeczpospolita [Feb 02], yet the WIG20TR ETF rose only 0.12% and KGHM keeps falling (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02) — Warsaw is trading global metals, not Polish growth.

Narrative: Tech is a two-speed sector: XLK rose 0.96% as AAPL jumped 4.06%, while MSFT fell 1.61% and ORCL 2.75% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Wall Street now openly talks about haves and have-nots in tech after earnings Yahoo Finance [Feb 02].

Reported: Palantir beat fourth-quarter estimates on the strength of AI and defense demand CNBC [Feb 02], the clearest counterexample to the 'software is dead' trade. Oracle's $25 billion bond sale helped ease fears of an AI debt wave Bloomberg.com [Feb 02], yet ORCL is down 18.22% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

EPS Upside Watch: Monetisers with a lowered bar: PLTR's beat CNBC [Feb 02] arrived with the stock down 11.97% over 20 sessions, and AAPL's 4.06% jump shows investors paying for record hardware demand despite memory costs (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Estimate revisions, not multiple expansion, can carry both.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The split is not hardware versus software but AI monetisation versus AI cost Yahoo Finance [Feb 02]: Palantir is growing revenue on AI demand while Oracle has to borrow to build. Own the monetisers and fund them from the financed-capex names.

Narrative: Communication services hinges on the week's platform prints: Alphabet and Amazon report alongside the delayed jobs data and more Warsh fallout Yahoo Finance [Feb 02]. GOOGL rose 1.68% to 343.69 and is up 9.06% over 20 sessions, while XLC slipped 0.34% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Reported: Disney shares fell despite streaming growth as the CEO decision nears WSJ [Feb 02], losing 7.4% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Legacy media is being valued on succession risk, not on the quarter.

EPS Upside Watch: Alphabet: search, YouTube and cloud all monetise AI directly, and the bar is a revenue-led beat rather than a capex headline. META slipped 1.41% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), so platform expectations are not stretched going in.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Disney's drop despite growth WSJ [Feb 02] shows old-media multiples are capped by governance, not demand. XLC is a bet on AI platforms; underweight legacy media through management transitions.

Narrative: Financials led the rebound: XLF rose 1.1%, BAC 1.56% and GS 1.17% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), mirroring the bank-led record in Europe Reuters [Feb 02]. A stronger ISM and a bear-steepening curve support loan growth and margins.

Reported: The micro news was a warning rather than a trend: Chicago's Metropolitan Capital Bank became the first US bank failure of 2026 Yahoo Finance [Feb 02]. JPM rose 0.74% to 308.14 but is still down 5.33% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

EPS Upside Watch: Capital-markets franchises: record-pace bond issuance (see the flows section) and recovering equity markets feed fees at GS and the large banks, whose shares lag the S&P 500's 1.72% 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The tail sits in private credit: UBS's worst case for AI disruption has private-credit defaults hitting 13% Bloomberg.com [Feb 02]. Own the money-centre banks, avoid BDCs with software-heavy books.

Narrative: The Iran premium is unwinding: oil settled down more than 4% on US-Iran de-escalation Reuters [Feb 02], with Brent down 6.21% to 66.30, WTI down 4.71% to 62.14, XLE down 1.96% and XOM down 2.12% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Reported: Exxon beat as Permian and Guyana fields took output to a 40-year high Reuters [Jan 30] — the majors' story is volume. XOM is still up 12.84% and CVX 11.63% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), gains built partly on a supply-shock premium now being negotiated away.

EPS Upside Watch: Gas is the downside surprise: US natural-gas prices plummeted on warmer forecasts Bloomberg.com [Feb 02], with Henry Hub down 25.65% to 3.24 in one session and 52.4% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Gas-weighted producers' first-quarter estimates are too high; refiners with cheaper feedstock are the relative winners.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Talks, not strikes: US-Iran nuclear talks are expected Friday Axios [Feb 02]. If they hold, Brent's remaining 9.14% 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02) is the next leg to unwind — the 'geopolitical floor' under oil is weaker than consensus assumes.

Narrative: Industrials are the macro winner: the January ISM rose to 52.6% PR Newswire [Feb 02] and industrials were among the leaders of Monday's rally CNBC [Feb 02]. CAT jumped 5.1% to 690.91 and XLI rose 1.26% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Reported: Results season for the big industrials is largely behind us; the read-through now comes from the data, with US factory activity posting its fastest gains since 2022 WSJ [Feb 02]. CAT is up 15.46% over 20 sessions and GE rose 0.63% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

EPS Upside Watch: Short-cycle names — machinery, distributors, transports — gain most from an ISM back above 50, and the Russell 2000 rose 1.02% to 2,640.28 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02) as investors began to price it. Defence primes add a second leg on European demand.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Breadth is the surprise: a manufacturing rebound WSJ [Feb 02] turns the AI-capex-only industrial trade into a cyclical one, which favours laggards such as BA, down 6.2% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Narrative: Discretionary is still K-shaped: the economy has turned restaurant winners and losers upside down, Business Insider reports Business Insider [Feb 02]. XLY rose 0.66% while TSLA fell 2.0% and HD rose 0.94% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Reported: Tyson topped estimates on strong chicken sales and its stock rose Barron's [Feb 02], while Disney's streaming growth did not save its shares WSJ [Feb 02]. Spending is holding up; share reactions diverge on company-specific issues.

EPS Upside Watch: Amazon headlines the busiest week of the reporting period with Alphabet CNBC [Feb 01]; AMZN rose 1.53% to 242.96 and is up 7.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). AWS growth and retail margins are the swing factors for a beat.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The K-shape Business Insider [Feb 02] means averages mislead: value chains and premium brands both win while the middle loses. Own the extremes and avoid mid-priced casual dining and mall retail.

Narrative: Staples keep winning the rotation: XLP rose 1.19% and is up 8.77% over 20 sessions, with WMT up 4.13% to 124.06 and COST 2.99% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Defensive demand survived even a strong-data day.

Reported: Tyson topped earnings estimates on strong chicken sales and the stock rose Barron's [Feb 02] — protein demand is resilient in a K-shaped consumer economy. XLV and XLP both rose in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), a sign defensives are not being sold to fund cyclicals.

EPS Upside Watch: Walmart and Costco are the price-makers: WMT is up 10.02% and COST 13.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), and both sit at the value end of the K-shaped consumer Business Insider [Feb 02].

⚡ Breaking Convention: Staples rallying on an ISM-surprise day is unusual — the bid looks like rotation money that can leave if cyclicals keep working. Trim XLP into strength if payrolls confirm the factory rebound PR Newswire [Feb 02].

Narrative: Healthcare is still the policy sector: XLV is up only 0.12% over 20 sessions while UNH is down 15.1% and LLY 3.35% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). PBMs were hit by a Trump transparency rule Axios [Feb 02], adding to the managed-care squeeze.

Reported: Revvity forecast 2026 profit and revenue above estimates after a blowout fourth quarter Reuters [Feb 02], so tools demand is not uniformly weak. UNH slipped 0.47% to 285.59 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

EPS Upside Watch: Obesity volume remains the sector's one clear estimate upside, and LLY rose 0.67% to 1,044.13 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Life-science tools are the second candidate after Revvity's guide Reuters [Feb 02].

⚡ Breaking Convention: PBM reform Axios [Feb 02] hurts the middlemen but can help drugmakers' net pricing — winners and losers sit inside the same sector. Short managed care and PBMs against long branded pharma.

Narrative: Materials split between a precious-metals unwind and a strategic-minerals bid: gold and silver fell further as a CME margin hike stoked selling CNBC [Feb 02], while Trump launched a $12 billion minerals stockpile to counter China Reuters [Feb 02]. XLB rose 0.77% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Reported: The tape, not results, set the tone: copper extended its slump as traders eyed volatility across metals Bloomberg.com [Feb 02], with the front month down 1.62% to 5.80, while FCX rose 0.88% and NEM 0.45% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

EPS Upside Watch: Critical-minerals producers: a $12 billion stockpile Reuters [Feb 02] creates a price-insensitive buyer for strategic minerals, an estimate tailwind that has not yet reached company guidance.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Consensus treats metals as one trade; the stockpile Reuters [Feb 02] splits them into state-backed demand for strategic minerals versus margin-driven liquidation in gold and silver CNBC [Feb 02]. Own the strategic producers, not the bullion proxies.
Narrative: REITs fell 1.13% as the 10Y rose to 4.29% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02; US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-02). A hotter ISM and a hawkish Fed pick push rate relief further out.

Reported: The credit signal is household stress: more homeowners are falling behind on their mortgages as affordability bites CNBC [Feb 02]. That is a risk for residential and mortgage REITs more than for data-centre landlords.

EPS Upside Watch: Data-centre and industrial landlords tied to the manufacturing upturn and the AI build-out keep pricing power, but XLRE's 1.44% 20-session gain lags the S&P 500's 1.72% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), so selection matters more than beta.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Rising mortgage stress CNBC [Feb 02] would eventually pull long yields down — the REIT bear case carries its own hedge. Pair an underweight in mortgage REITs with a small long in long-duration Treasuries.

Narrative: Utilities lost the defensive bid: XLU fell 1.46% and is down 1.3% over 20 sessions, while CEG fell 3.49% and VST 2.58% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Higher yields and collapsing gas prices both hurt.

Reported: The EIA says US wholesale day-ahead electricity prices rose in 2025 with higher natural-gas prices U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) (.gov) [Feb 02] — the tailwind merchant generators rode. With Henry Hub down 25.65% in a session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), that tailwind is reversing.

EPS Upside Watch: Regulated names with rate-base growth hold up best: NEE is still up 6.67% over 20 sessions despite a 1.79% drop (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Contracted data-centre load matters more than spot power prices.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Cheap gas is bullish for data-centre economics and for industrial power users, but bearish for the stocks that sold the AI-power story: CEG is down 26.04% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). The AI-power trade is migrating from generators to equipment makers.

Narrative: European autos bounced with the market — the SXAP tracker rose 0.72% — but remain down 4.29% over 20 sessions, with Renault down 10.48% and Stellantis 13.31% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Chinese competition and EV price wars have not gone away.

Reported: European automakers are rethinking software independence Automotive News [Feb 02], a strategic retreat after years of in-house platform spending. BMW rose 0.66% and Mercedes 1.09% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).
EPS Upside Watch: A firmer dollar helps: EUR/USD fell 0.97% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), a translation tailwind for German premium brands' US sales if it persists.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Partnering on software Automotive News [Feb 02] could cut capex faster than the market expects — the bear case assumes Europe keeps spending to compete alone. VOW3, down only 0.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), is the relative winner if costs fall.

Narrative: Semis rebounded: SOXX rose 1.85%, MU 5.52%, INTC 5.04% and TSM 3.27% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). TrendForce sees chip prices surging 90-95% in the first quarter from the previous quarter Reuters [Feb 02] — the memory cycle is now about price, not just volume.

Reported: NXP forecast an upbeat quarter, signalling an industrial market bottom Reuters [Feb 02], and Sandisk rocketed another 16% TradingView [Feb 02]. Nvidia shares fell after a report that its OpenAI investment stalled CNBC [Feb 02], ending 2.89% lower (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

EPS Upside Watch: Memory and storage: a 90-95% first-quarter chip price jump Reuters [Feb 02] flows almost straight to margins, and MU is up 38.8% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02) as estimates chase. Analog names gain from the industrial bottom NXP flagged Reuters [Feb 02].

⚡ Breaking Convention: The GPU leader is the laggard: NVDA is down 1.72% over 20 sessions while MU is up 38.8% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Scarcity, not share, drives returns — own memory and equipment over the accelerator crowd, and treat any memory-price rollover as the signal to rotate back.

Rewarded: Pricing power and proven demand: Sandisk rocketed another 16% TradingView [Feb 02], Tyson rose after beating on chicken sales Barron's [Feb 02], and AAPL jumped 4.06% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Palantir, beating on AI and defense demand CNBC [Feb 02], and NXP, with an upbeat guide Reuters [Feb 02], reported after the close and are the next tests of whether beats get paid.

Punished: Disney fell despite streaming growth WSJ [Feb 02] — governance trumped the quarter — and the AI spenders kept bleeding: MSFT is down 10.48% and ORCL 18.22% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Even a $25 billion bond sale that eased AI-debt fears Bloomberg.com [Feb 02] did not lift Oracle's stock.

Pattern: Wall Street sees a divide between tech haves and have-nots after earnings Yahoo Finance [Feb 02]: revenue that proves AI demand is rewarded, capex that must be financed is not. A beat alone is not enough; the reaction follows whether the print changes the funding or growth story. Governance can override both, as Disney's succession overhang showed in the same session.

Attention into EPS: Alphabet and Amazon report in a week that also carries more Warsh fallout Yahoo Finance [Feb 02], Yahoo Finance previews AMD's quarter Yahoo Finance [Feb 02], and the jobs report will be delayed Reuters [Feb 02] — so earnings, not payrolls, set the macro tone. Alphabet must show cloud acceleration; AMD must address accelerator timing.

Playbook: Buy monetisers on post-earnings dips (PLTR, memory) and fade financed-capex stories until free cash flow stabilises. Stop the long-monetiser, short-spender pair if MSFT reclaims 472.94, its close 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Attention Gap: The January ISM jumped to 52.6% PR Newswire [Feb 02], the fastest gains since 2022 WSJ [Feb 02], yet hedge funds have been trimming North America exposure amid trade tensions, dollar pain and megacap weakness Reuters [Feb 02]. The money is leaving US megacaps just as the data turn in favour of domestic cyclicals those funds are not chasing.

Exposure & Risk: Express via IWM (262.18, up 5.39% over 20 sessions) and XLI (167.53) rather than megacaps (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Risk: one survey is not a cycle, payrolls are delayed Reuters [Feb 02], and a hawkish Fed would hit small caps' floating-rate debt first.

Attention Gap: A two-thirds majority for the LDP-JIP coalition The Japan Times [Feb 02] plus a BOJ worried about being behind the curve Reuters [Feb 01] is a rate-and-spending mix. Attention is on the yen; the cleaner beneficiary is bank net interest income.

Exposure & Risk: Express via MUFG, SMFG and Mizuho ADRs while hedging the yen, given USD/JPY's 1.33% one-day rise to 155.20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Risk: a JGB selloff if fiscal promises spook bond investors Reuters [Feb 02], which would hit bank bond books before it lifts margins.

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was 78,688.77, up 2.23% on the day but down 11.77% over five sessions and 17.45% over 20; ether closed at 2,344.36, down 22.03% over five, and solana at 104.47, down 28.13% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). In US trading IBIT fell 6.89% to 44.22, MSTR 6.73% and COIN 3.53% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Bitcoin briefly tumbled below $75K, though some investors see a buying opportunity MarketWatch [Feb 02].

New / Most Important: Strategy slid after bitcoin briefly dipped below the firm's key breakeven level CNBC [Feb 02], and crypto-exchange stocks have lost more than 55% on a retail exodus Bloomberg.com [Feb 02]. Policy is stuck too: the stablecoin-yield deadlock persists in White House talks between banks and crypto firms Bloomberg.com [Feb 02]. The exchange drawdown is a volume story — retail activity, not just prices, is shrinking, which removes the marginal buyer that powered last year's rallies.

Playbook: Stay underweight crypto equities; the weakest link is leverage at treasury companies trading near their bitcoin cost. Use IBIT for any re-entry and only after bitcoin holds above $75K on daily closes MarketWatch [Feb 02]; a stablecoin compromise Bloomberg.com [Feb 02] is the policy catalyst that would change the call.

Rates & Dollar: The dollar advanced on safe-haven flows and strong US data Reuters [Feb 02]: the DXY rose 0.64% to 97.61 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). The 10Y closed at 4.29% and the 30Y at 4.90%, with the 10Y up 7 bps over five observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-02), while TLT fell 0.67% to 86.55 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Credit Check: Supply is enormous but clearing: global bond sales reached $1 trillion at their fastest pace ever Bloomberg.com [Feb 02], and Oracle's $25 billion deal eased fears of an AI debt wave Bloomberg.com [Feb 02]. HYG slipped 0.43% and LQD 0.46% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02); the stress is in private credit, where UBS's worst case puts AI-related defaults at 13% Bloomberg.com [Feb 02].

Portfolio Implication: Hold equities over bonds while issuance clears and the ISM improves; keep duration short and IG in the front end, where carry is decent and supply pressure is lighter. A failed or heavily discounted AI mega-deal would be the signal to cut credit beta; until then the cheapest hedge is the long-dollar sleeve that rallied on the strong data Reuters [Feb 02].

What Is Priced: Market experts are pricing higher odds of a cash-rate increase Mortgage Professional America [Feb 02] at Tuesday's meeting ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation [Jan 29], a U-turn against the global easing trend Bloomberg.com [Feb 01]. AUD/USD is still up 3.93% over 20 sessions at 0.6946 despite a 1.43% drop in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Conditional Expression: Hike with a hawkish statement: buy AUD on the dip, own Australian bank margins, and underweight REITs and housing-linked retailers. Hold: sell AUD toward 0.6684, its level 20 sessions earlier, and buy ASX rate-sensitives on relief (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Risk: A hike framed as one-and-done would leave AUD longs exposed, and the ASX 200 is up only 0.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), so equities have little cushion for a hawkish surprise.

What Is Priced: Oil has already priced de-escalation: it settled down more than 4% on easing supply worries Reuters [Feb 02], with Brent down 6.21% to 66.30 and USO down 5.27% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Nuclear talks are expected Friday amid a US military buildup Axios [Feb 02].

Conditional Expression: Talks progress: short Brent rallies and underweight upstream energy in favour of airlines and refiners. Talks collapse: Brent's 9.14% 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02) can rebuild quickly, so hold upside calls on USO as cheap protection and keep upstream exposure in volume-growth producers rather than high-cost names.
Risk: The military buildup Axios [Feb 02] means talks can fail into a strike — the asymmetric outcome. Keep any short-oil position small and hedged through Friday.

Catalyst & Thesis: Palantir beat fourth-quarter estimates on AI and defense demand CNBC [Feb 02], with a 70% revenue jump, per Forbes Forbes [Feb 02]. A company whose revenue is accelerating on AI should de-couple from the seat-based SaaS selloff, and the print is the evidence.

Price Hurdle & Risk: PLTR closed at 147.76 before the report, up 0.8% on the day but down 11.97% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). The hurdle is 167.86, the close 20 sessions earlier; the risk is that valuation, not growth, caps the reaction — exit if the stock gives back its post-print move below 147.76.

Catalyst & Thesis: Alphabet reports in a week that also carries the delayed jobs data and Warsh fallout Yahoo Finance [Feb 02]. It sits on the right side of the haves-and-have-nots split Yahoo Finance [Feb 02]: AI that monetises through search, YouTube and cloud rather than capex that needs outside funding.

Price Hurdle & Risk: GOOGL closed at 343.69, up 1.68% on the day and 9.06% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Risk: a capex guide that outruns cloud growth would put it in Microsoft's camp; cut on a close below 315.15, the level 20 sessions earlier.

Catalyst & Thesis: Yahoo Finance previews what Wall Street expects from AMD's fourth quarter Yahoo Finance [Feb 02]. With chip prices seen surging 90-95% in the first quarter Reuters [Feb 02], memory costs rise for accelerator makers, and any slip in the MI450 ramp would show up in 2026 guidance.

Price Hurdle & Risk: AMD jumped 4.03% to 246.27 in the prior session and is up 10.2% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02); the downside target is 223.47, the close 20 sessions earlier. Cover if management confirms the MI450 timeline and holds margin guidance.

Observed Attention: CNBC reports retail traders aren't giving up on SLV even after silver's plunge CNBC [Feb 02]. SLV fell another 3.98% to 72.44 and is down 26.34% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Motivation & Bias: Anchoring to January's highs and the debasement narrative keep buyers averaging down. A CME margin hike that stoked further selling CNBC [Feb 02] is exactly the kind of forced flow retail rarely anticipates.

Instrument & Risk: SLV is still up 10.17% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), so the January gain has not fully unwound. Use defined-risk call spreads instead of shares, and size for margin-driven volatility.

Observed Attention: Stocktwits says MSTR and BMNR felt the heat even as bitcoin recovered to $77,000, with crypto facing an over-$800 million liquidation wave Stocktwits [Feb 02]. Retail chatter keeps centring on the treasury companies rather than on the coins.

Motivation & Bias: Retail treats the treasury companies as levered dip-buys; with Strategy trading near its bitcoin breakeven CNBC [Feb 02], the equity premium is what evaporates first. That is authority bias meeting a balance-sheet test.

Instrument & Risk: MSTR fell 6.73% to 139.63 and is down 13.05% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Prefer IBIT for crypto beta; the treasury equities carry funding risk that the coin does not.
Observed Attention: Sandisk rocketed another 16% in a single session, with analysts seeing further upside TradingView [Feb 02]. It has become one of the purest momentum vehicles for the memory cycle.

Motivation & Bias: Momentum chasing is backed by a real price story — chip prices are seen surging 90-95% in the first quarter Reuters [Feb 02] — which makes this fundamentals-plus-FOMO, a mix that can overshoot both ways.

Instrument & Risk: SNDK is not on our card; MU, at 437.80 and up 38.8% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), is the more liquid proxy. Use trailing stops rather than fixed targets; a rollover in memory prices is the exit signal.
Observed Attention: WSJ reports Cboe is in talks to bring back all-or-nothing options to vie with prediction markets WSJ [Feb 02], a direct bid for the retail flow that has moved into event betting.

Motivation & Bias: Binary payoffs suit lottery-style preferences — a small stake for a big payoff — the same behaviour that drove retail into silver and crypto proxies. Exchanges are building products to follow that demand.

Instrument & Risk: No card price for Cboe. The investable angle is the venue rather than the bets: listed exchanges gain from retail volume, while regulatory pushback on event contracts is the main risk.

Market data: Yahoo Finance, prior completed sessions; Treasury curve: US Treasury daily par yields. Changes are price changes, not total returns. Currency sessions follow exchange-local dates; crypto observations include weekends.
